question: A 75-year-old woman is being treated for atrial fibrillation. She presents to the clinic with complaints of nausea, vomiting, photophobia, and yellow-green vision with yellow halos around the lights. She has a heart rate of 64/min, blood pressure is 118/76 mm Hg, and respiratory rate is 15/min. Physical examination reveals regular heart sounds with clear lung sounds bilaterally. Liver function tests are normal. Toxicity of which of the following anti-arrhythmic drugs would best fit this clinical picture?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Yellow-green vision with yellow halos around lights" -> "Xanthopsia" -> "Characteristic of digoxin toxicity" -> 95% CHAIN: "Nausea, vomiting, photophobia" -> "Symptoms of digoxin toxicity" -> "Suggestive of digoxin overdose" -> 90% CHAIN: "Atrial fibrillation treatment" -> "Digoxin commonly used" -> "Likely drug in this scenario" -> 95%
enhanced_information: The clinical presentation of a 75-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation showing symptoms of nausea, vomiting, photophobia, yellow-green vision with yellow halos around lights, along with normal liver function tests, is highly suggestive of digoxin toxicity. The symptoms align with known manifestations of digoxin overdose. The evidence paths linking nausea, vomiting, and photophobia to digoxin further support this conclusion.
analysis: The clinical presentation of a 75-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation exhibiting symptoms of nausea, vomiting, photophobia, yellow-green vision with yellow halos around lights, along with normal liver function tests, strongly suggests digoxin toxicity. These symptoms are classic manifestations of digoxin overdose. Other anti-arrhythmic drugs are less likely to cause this specific constellation of symptoms.
